The strongest aspect is the centrality of the subject matter. Method classes are extremely important for social sciences. The subject is also easier to conduct via zoom than via face-to-face interactions. So the subject is easy to study from home. 
However, the weakest points relate to the high number of students from diverse backgrounds. Normally, diversity is not a problem on its own especially since the class is at introductory level. However, graduate students from my department have no alternative methods courses and would appreciate a more specialized methods course. This course was tiered more towards the Pscyhology department (e.g. datasets). This did not hinder the effectiveness of teaching, of course, but the logic of causal inference may differ according to departments as well. The distribution of this course into separate seminar groups/classes would suffice. It is not the weakness of this particular course per se to be the only methods course available to a huge number of students, but the weakness of the faculty.

Professor Mouratidis has been a very effective instructor who has always tried his best to teach us all we need to know about research in psychology. He comes to the classes with a bunch of paper (in which he brings scientific articles, examples and class activities)  in his hands and in each class, he had actually worked with us, challenged us to learn, and to learn by actually putting an effort. He created an class environment in which everybody can participate and discuss their opinions. Even I, as being someone with a  social anxiety, have felt that I can participate without worrying about humiliation or making a mistake because I knew that even if I say/do something wrong, the teacher wants us to learn and do better, so he will correct us in a receptive and respectful manner. I think we need more teachers like him.
